name: Ratios in similar figures
formula: \text{length ratio } k \implies \text{area ratio } k^2, \quad \text{volume ratio } k^3
whenToUse: Two figures are similar, such as a triangle cut by a line parallel to a side, or a cone cut parallel to its base, and you need an area or a volume.
example: A line parallel to the base of a triangle of area $50$ cuts off a top triangle whose sides are $\frac{2}{5}$ of the original. Its area is $\frac{4}{25} \cdot 50 = 8$, so the trapezoid below has area $42$.
pitfall: Do not apply the length ratio to areas or volumes. Also the ratio is between matching parts of the WHOLE small figure and the WHOLE large figure, not the leftover piece.
